cells.reason: Singapore Food Regulations Tenth Schedule (b)(15), arsenic column, sets 1 ppm total arsenic for 'fish, crustaceans, and molluscs' with no species or habitat carve-out, so freshwater tilapia, catfish, trout and carp are within scope; basis 'product as sold or imported' is food content and coincides with as-consumed for raw or frozen fish. The informal consolidation is in force from 30 January 2026 (regulation 31 prohibition). No non-gated tAs food-content row covering fish is stricter: GY 200 is quarantined, PY and MERCOSUR 'raw, frozen, or refrigerated fish' are equal at 1000, AU-NZ fish is 2000, TT 5000, IN 76000.

The same Tenth Schedule row names crustaceans and molluscs expressly, and bivalves are molluscs, so uncanned shellfish is squarely within 'fish, crustaceans, and molluscs' at 1 ppm total arsenic on the product as sold. Instrument in force from 30 January 2026, content basis. No non-gated same-analyte row is stricter: AU-NZ molluscs 1000 and the PY/MERCOSUR crustacean, bivalve and cephalopod rows at 1000 are equal, HK regulates only inorganic arsenic for aquatic animals other than fish, and MX 80000 and IN 86000 are far looser.
